orders.reason: Elective cholecystectomy for chronic gallstone pancreatitis

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Winter check-in, slow season at work. Feels fully back to himself after the endocarditis. Weight back to baseline. Cardiology echo 10/20 clean: no residual vegetation, MVP with mild MR, normal LV.

GI: on Creon with every meal/snack, omeprazole daily. No abdominal pain episodes. Stools fine.

Meds: Creon 36,000 w/ meals + snacks, ASA 81, omeprazole 20, amoxicillin 2 g pre-dental.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine - pseudocholinesterase deficiency (homozygous atypical).

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Heart regular, apical systolic murmur unchanged. Lungs clear. Abd obese, soft, nontender, no Murphy sign. No edema.

A/P:
1. Chronic gallstone pancreatitis, gallbladder in situ - the stones are what started this, and leaving the gallbladder in keeps the door open for more attacks. He is ready now. Referral to general surgery for elective lap chole. Will make sure anesthesia knows about the cholinesterase deficiency.
2. Hypoalbuminemia - recheck today.
3. MVP/mild MR, s/p mitral IE - stable, prophylaxis before dental work.
4. Obesity - weight back to baseline.

RTC April physical.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Albumin back to 3.4, other labs normal. Surgery referral is in - their office should call you within a couple of weeks.

reports.text: Regional hospital imaging. Ordered by general surgery. Liver normal in size and echotexture, no focal lesion. Gallbladder contains multiple mobile shadowing gallstones. Gallbladder wall is not thickened; no pericholecystic fluid; sonographic Murphy sign negative. Common bile duct normal in caliber. Pancreas partly obscured by bowel gas; visualized portions unremarkable. Right kidney normal.
reports.conclusion: Cholelithiasis without sonographic evidence of acute cholecystitis. Normal common bile duct caliber.

documents.title: General Surgery Consultation
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Outside general surgery practice. Visit 02/16/2026.

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for referring Mr. Coughlin, 46, with chronic pancreatitis attributed to gallstones, gallbladder still in place, on pancreatic enzyme replacement. Currently asymptomatic. Ultrasound 02/09 shows multiple gallstones with a normal wall and a normal-caliber duct.

History reviewed including mitral valve endocarditis in 2025 (treated, resolved), MVP with mild MR, and pseudocholinesterase deficiency with prolonged paralysis after succinylcholine in 2024.

Exam: obese abdomen, soft, nontender, no hernia. Healed right thigh incision.

Impression: cholelithiasis with gallstone-related chronic pancreatitis.
Plan: elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy, booked 06/08/2026 at his request (around his work schedule). Preoperative evaluation with PCP within 30 days of surgery. Anesthesia preoperative clinic aware of the cholinesterase deficiency; succinylcholine will be avoided.

Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine (prolonged apnea).

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Omeprazole refill please. Also surgery is June 8, they said I need to see you before.

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Refill sent. Pre-op visit booked Tue 5/26 at 7:30. Physical is still on for 4/20.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit. Busy season starting at work, feels well. Surgery consult done: lap chole set for 6/8. Pre-op with me 5/26.

ROS negative: no fevers, sweats, chest pain, dyspnea, abdominal pain, change in stools, urinary complaints, mood problems.

Meds: Creon 36,000 w/ meals + snacks, ASA 81, omeprazole 20, amoxicillin 2 g pre-dental (used once for a cleaning in March).
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine (pseudocholinesterase deficiency).
SH: still not smoking. A few beers on weekends. Riding again this spring.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight stable. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes or thyromegaly. Heart regular, apical systolic murmur unchanged. Lungs clear. Abd obese, soft, nontender. Skin fine. No edema.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance - FIT kit given (last year negative). Lipids, A1c, CBC, CMP. PHQ-9 1. Tdap 2025, flu and covid done in the fall. Shingles vaccine at 50.
2. Chronic gallstone pancreatitis - surgery booked.
3. Hypoalbuminemia - recheck.
4. MVP/mild MR, prior IE - stable.
5. Obesity - stable.

documents.title: FIT and physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. April labs normal, albumin 3.4 unchanged. Pt notified by portal. Next FIT spring 2027.

reports.text: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis. Normal intervals. No ST or T wave abnormality.

documents.title: Preoperative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pre-op for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy 6/8/2026, outside general surgery.

Functional capacity good: walks job sites and climbs ladders all day, more than 4 METs without symptoms. No chest pain, dyspnea, syncope, palpitations. No bleeding history. Only prior anesthetic was 12/2024 (femur fixation) complicated by prolonged paralysis after succinylcholine; workup showed homozygous atypical pseudocholinesterase deficiency.

PMH: chronic gallstone pancreatitis on enzymes, MVP with mild MR, mitral valve endocarditis 2025 (viridans strep, treated, resolved on 10/2025 echo), hypoalbuminemia, obesity, R femur ORIF 2024. Former smoker.
Meds: Creon 36,000 w/ meals + snacks, ASA 81, omeprazole 20, amoxicillin 2 g pre-dental.
Allergies/alerts: SUCCINYLCHOLINE - prolonged apnea (pseudocholinesterase deficiency). Also avoid mivacurium.

Exam: vitals as charted. Airway: normal mouth opening, full neck range. Heart regular, apical systolic murmur unchanged. Lungs clear. Abd obese, soft, nontender. No edema.
ECG: normal sinus rhythm, normal.
Labs: CBC, BMP today.

Assessment: low-to-intermediate risk procedure, good functional capacity, no active cardiac condition. Acceptable to proceed.
Recommendations:
- Anesthesia: no succinylcholine or mivacurium. Letter to anesthesia and surgery sent with the 12/2024 cholinesterase report.
- Endocarditis prophylaxis is not indicated for this GI procedure.
- Aspirin: per surgeon.
- Continue Creon with meals once eating.

Copy to general surgery and anesthesia preoperative clinic.

results.text: Normal respiratory flora; no pathogens isolated

reports.text: Portable AP view, postoperative day 1, increasing dyspnea and hypoxia. Bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. Heart size normal. No pneumothorax. No large pleural effusion.
Specimen: gallbladder, laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Gross: opened gallbladder containing multiple gallstones. Microscopic: gallbladder wall with chronic inflammation. No dysplasia or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Cholelithiasis; gallbladder with chronic inflammation; negative for dysplasia and malignancy.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - General Surgery / Critical Care
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 06/08/2026, discharged 06/17/2026.

Procedure 06/08/2026: elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for cholelithiasis with gallstone-related chronic pancreatitis. Completed without immediate complication. Anesthesia: known homozygous atypical pseudocholinesterase deficiency; succinylcholine avoided, a non-depolarizing relaxant used and fully reversed before extubation.

Postoperative course: tachypnea and hypoxia developed after surgery; transferred to the ICU on postoperative day 1 (06/09). On ICU arrival afebrile, respiratory rate 28, SpO2 92% on room air, with crackles throughout both lung fields. POD 1 labs: WBC 12.0, Hgb 13.5, platelets 250, creatinine 1.0, BNP 50. ABG pH 7.48, PaCO2 32, PaO2 70. Portable chest film: bilateral infiltrates. With normal BNP and normal LV function on prior echo, a cardiogenic cause was felt unlikely; diagnosis acute respiratory distress syndrome.

Oxygenation worsened over the day despite high-flow nasal oxygen and he was intubated the evening of 06/09. Lung-protective ventilation; worst PaO2/FiO2 108 on PEEP 14. Prone positioning was used. Cisatracurium infusion for 48 hours for ventilator synchrony (not dependent on plasma cholinesterase). Conservative fluid strategy. Blood and respiratory cultures negative. No clear precipitant was identified. Oxygenation improved steadily; extubated 06/13, transferred out of the ICU 06/14, weaned to room air, discharged home 06/17.

Pathology: cholelithiasis, chronic inflammation of the gallbladder wall, no dysplasia or malignancy.

Discharge diagnoses: ARDS after laparoscopic cholecystectomy, resolving; status post cholecystectomy; chronic pancreatitis; MVP with mild MR; history of mitral valve endocarditis (2025); pseudocholinesterase deficiency; hypoalbuminemia; obesity.
Discharge medications: pancrelipase with meals and snacks, aspirin 81 mg daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily; amoxicillin before dental work as before.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; chest imaging in 4-6 weeks; pulmonology clinic. Surgery clinic 2 weeks for wound check.

Note: hospital course details from the critical care team are summarized above.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt 2 days after discharge. Home, short of breath on the stairs but better each day, fine at rest. Port sites healing, no drainage, no fever. Eating small meals, taking Creon. Bought a pulse oximeter, readings ok at rest. Told him to go to the ED if breathing gets worse, chest pain, or oximeter in the 80s. TCM visit Mon 6/22 8am.

events.reason: Hospital follow-up after cholecystectomy and ARDS

orders.reason: Follow-up of bilateral infiltrates after ARDS

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Elective lap chole 6/8, then ARDS starting POD 1: ICU, intubated 6/9-6/13, proned, no cause found, home on room air 6/17. Discharge summary reviewed in full. Succinylcholine was avoided as planned.

Now: breathing better daily, winded on a flight of stairs, fine walking on level ground. No cough to speak of, no fever, no chest pain, no leg swelling. Port sites sore but fine. Appetite low, eating small meals with Creon. Down 4 kg from pre-op.

Meds: Creon 36,000 w/ meals + snacks, ASA 81, omeprazole 20, amoxicillin 2 g pre-dental.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine.

Exam: vitals as charted, sat ok on room air at rest. Tired appearing. Lungs: clear today, no crackles. Heart regular, apical systolic murmur unchanged. Abd soft, port sites clean and dry, no erythema. Calves soft, nontender. No edema.

A/P:
1. ARDS after lap chole, recovering - CXR in about 3 weeks; referral to pulmonology for follow-up. Walk daily, build up slowly. Return precautions reviewed.
2. S/p cholecystectomy - surgery wound check next week.
3. Hypoalbuminemia - expected dip after ICU; recheck today and again in 2 months. Protein shakes again.
4. Work - off; FMLA paperwork to front desk. Target return decided after pulm visit.
5. Chronic pancreatitis - continue enzymes.

documents.title: FMLA forms
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: FMLA certification from employer HR received by fax. Completed by PCP: continuous leave from 6/8/2026, reassess after pulmonology visit. Faxed back to HR, copy scanned, pt notified.

reports.text: PA and lateral. Comparison portable chest 06/09/2026. Near-complete clearing of the previously seen bilateral opacities. No new consolidation. Heart size normal. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Cholecystectomy clips in the right upper quadrant.

documents.title: Chest X-ray
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Brett, your chest X-ray yesterday looks much better - the haziness from the ARDS has almost completely cleared. That fits with how you're feeling. Keep the pulmonology appointment on the 27th.

documents.title: RE: Chest X-ray
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good. Walking 2 miles now. Stairs still get me a little.

documents.title: Pulmonary Clinic Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group. Visit 07/27/2026.

Dear Doctor,

I saw Mr. Coughlin, 47, about seven weeks after ARDS that began the day after an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy (intubated 06/09-06/13, prone positioning, no precipitant found, cultures negative). Former smoker, quit at 42.

He is improving steadily: walking two miles, still breathless on more than a flight of stairs, no cough, no chest pain, no orthopnea.

Exam: comfortable, room air saturation normal, lungs clear, no clubbing, no edema.
Chest X-ray 07/13: near-complete clearing.

Impression: ARDS, resolved, with expected recovery of exercise tolerance still under way.
Plan: graded return to activity; may return to work on light duty now, full duty in about a month if he keeps improving. Return to clinic in 3 months; sooner with any setback.

Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u. Back on light duty (site office, no ladders) since pulmonology visit 7/27. Pulm called the ARDS resolved; CXR 7/13 nearly clear. Stairs better, still the last thing to come back. No cough, no fever. Eating normally, weight coming back up. Surgery released him at the wound check.

GI: Creon with meals, stools ok, no pain since surgery.

Meds: Creon 36,000 w/ meals + snacks, ASA 81, omeprazole 20, amoxicillin 2 g pre-dental.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine (pseudocholinesterase deficiency).

Exam: vitals as charted. Looks like himself. Lungs clear. Heart regular, apical systolic murmur unchanged. Abd soft, port scars healed. No edema.

A/P:
1. ARDS, resolved - full duty per pulm in a few weeks if stairs keep improving; pulm f/u in the fall.
2. Hypoalbuminemia - CMP today. Has been low on and off for two years; with chronic pancreatitis on enzymes, checking vitamin D too.
3. S/p cholecystectomy, chronic pancreatitis - continue Creon, omeprazole.
4. MVP/mild MR, prior IE - stable.
5. Flu shot next visit when the new vaccine is in.

RTC 4 weeks.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kidney and liver tests normal. Albumin 3.3, back up from 3.0 in June. Vitamin D is a send-out and will take a few more days; I'll let you know.
